_comment: Extra Bluetooth keys. Edit and the server picks changes up automatically (no firmware reflash). page: keyboard (usage 1-0xF1) or consumer (usage 1-0x3FF). group 'extra' shows the key in the TV controls grid; group 'pad' shows it in the top-left cell of the direction pad. Common consumer usages: Home 0x223, Menu 0x40, Volume Up 0xE9, Volume Down 0xEA, Mute 0xE2, Play/Pause 0xCD, Power 0x30, Next 0xB5, Previous 0xB6.

keys.label: Xiaomi input
keys._note: No documented HID code for the Xiaomi INPUT button exists. 'variants' are candidates the web button cycles through (tap = send the current one, long-press = switch to the next; the choice is remembered in the browser). Once one works, put it in 'hid' and delete 'variants'. Keyboard F24 (0x73) comes from a Xiaomi stick remote's Kodi log (scancode 0xc2 = KEY_F24); Consumer 0xB2 was tried first and did nothing. Appended from github.com/fanxeon/mi-ao docs/USAGE_EN.md (Xiaomi Remote 2 Pro fw 2671, vendor 0x2717 product 0x32B8): Back = keyboard 0xF1 (confirmed there), TV button = keyboard 0x35; its button list has no INPUT button, so the TV key is the likely candidate. Power = keyboard 0x66 is deliberately not offered here because it would switch the TV off. Appended from github.com/zmyisme/dsh-xiaomi-remote-2-pro (docs/EVIDENCE.md, lib/keys.js): Remote 2 Pro (VID 0x2717 / PID 0x32B8) is a keyboard-only HID device (no Consumer collection); INPUT/'TV' = keyboard 0x35 (marked an inference, not measured there) with an alternate firmware set using 0xC0. Same table: Home 0x4A, Menu 0x65, Back 0xF1, Vol+ 0x80, Vol- 0x81, Mute 0x7F, Power 0x66.
